clue.text: Energy producers deal with constant depression

indicators.note: in a down clue a depression is a letter being pushed lower, so the constant sinks from the top of the word to the bottom

parts.note: to deal with something is to cope
C is the usual symbol for a constant, such as the speed of light

explanation.surface: Power companies strike an agreement while weathering a long economic slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depression' is the move signal: in a down entry the C of COPE drops from the top to the bottom, giving OPEC.
explanation.definitionFit: OPEC is the cartel of petroleum-exporting nations, suppliers of oil and so of energy.

clue.text: Hard worker making veiled threat to PC?

definitions.meaning: someone who works like a ... labours tirelessly
a ... horse is malicious software disguised as something harmless that attacks a computer

explanation.surface: A diligent employee makes a thinly disguised threat to a police constable.
explanation.walkthrough: PC looks like police constable but here means personal computer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the Trojans: their endurance in the idiom, their wooden horse trick in the malware name.

clue.text: Parties forbid abstentions, each admitting vote's close

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the last letter of vote goes inside the word for forbid

parts.note: to forbid is to ban

indicators.note: the close of the word vote is its final letter
each says the same admission happens to the second word too, so it also takes in that letter

parts.note: fasts are periods of abstaining from food

explanation.surface: Political parties prohibit members from abstaining, with each vote taken to its conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'each admitting' means the E (the end of 'vote's') goes into both BAN and FASTS, making BEAN and FEASTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A beanfeast is an informal British word for a celebratory party or jolly outing.

clue.text: Foreign worker's phoned appeal to father in Paris?

indicators.note: a phoned message is heard rather than read, so the spoken words stand for the entry

parts.note: an appeal is the exclamation O, and a Parisian father is a père, so the phrase is O père

explanation.surface: A worker from abroad telephones an appeal to her dad in France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'O père' said aloud matches the French phrase for a live-in helper; 's is a link (is).
explanation.definitionFit: An au pair is a young person from abroad who lives with a family and helps with childcare.

clue.text: Behind time, heading off in high spirits

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, which is taken away here

parts.note: to do something behind time is to do it belatedly

explanation.surface: Running late, someone sets off cheerfully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' removes the first letter, B, from BELATEDLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in high spirits means acting joyfully and with elation, an adverbial phrase matching an adverb.

clue.text: Medical check barely sufficient (time lacking)

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so the letter for time is removed

parts.note: a scant amount is barely enough

explanation.surface: A health examination that was only just adequate because the doctor was short of time.
explanation.definitionFit: A scan is an imaging examination, such as ultrasound or MRI, used in medicine.

clue.text: Nevada city girl entertaining star

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to hold them within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: lass is a word for a girl
Vega is a bright star in the constellation Lyra

explanation.surface: A showgirl performs for a celebrity in the Nevada resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Las Vegas is the largest city in the US state of Nevada, famous for casinos.

clue.text: Famous Swiss count

definitions.meaning: William ... is the legendary Swiss marksman and folk hero
to ... is an old sense of counting, as in ... beads or a bank teller

explanation.definitionFit: William Tell is the archer of Swiss legend, and telling meant counting, as in a bank teller.

clue.text: Re plan: clear up date using this?

definitions.text: Re plan: clear up date using this?

indicators.note: the question invites us to rework all the preceding letters into the thing being used

explanation.surface: A note about rescheduling: sort out a date with the help of this.
explanation.walkthrough: All the letters of 'Re plan clear up date' are rearranged; the whole clue also describes the answer's use.
explanation.definitionFit: A perpetual calendar shows the weekday of any date in any year, handy for planning.

clue.text: The latest thing notorious 16 announced

indicators.note: something announced is spoken aloud, so the entry is what the phrase sounds like

parts.note: 16 is TWINS, and the notorious twins are the Krays, London gangsters of the 1960s

explanation.surface: The newest fashion was revealed by a pair of infamous twins.
explanation.walkthrough: Ronnie and Reggie Kray were twin gangsters in 1960s London; their surname sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A craze is a short-lived fashion or enthusiasm, the newest fad everyone is following.

clue.text: Louisianan prison guards just reduced by half

indicators.note: a guard surrounds what it protects, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: the can is slang for prison

indicators.note: only the first half of the word just is kept

explanation.surface: A Louisiana jail keeps its inmates, though only half of them deserve it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cajuns are descendants of French Acadian settlers living in Louisiana.

clue.text: Worker organised love-in, not a normal story

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's standard worker

indicators.note: organised means put in a new arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An employee arranged a hippy love-in, which made an unusual tale.
explanation.definitionFit: An antinovel deliberately abandons conventional fiction features like plot and character.

clue.text: Lots of notice for this amount of work

parts.note: lots means many
to give ear to something is to pay heed, so ear means notice or attention

explanation.surface: A long notice period is needed for a job of this size.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-year is a unit measuring the work one person does in a year.

clue.text: Ex-PM runs over press turning up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over
to press is to jam, squeeze tightly

explanation.surface: A former prime minister rushes past journalists who are arriving.
explanation.walkthrough: John Major was UK prime minister 1990-97. 'turning up' reverses ROJAM.
explanation.definitionFit: John Major served as British prime minister in the 1990s, so he is a former premier.

clue.text: Current type of beer

definitions.meaning: a current of air through a room
beer drawn from a cask rather than a bottle

explanation.definitionFit: A draught is both a flow of cold air indoors and beer served from the barrel.

clue.text: One cream primarily applied to injured patients?

definitions.text: One cream primarily applied to injured patients?

indicators.note: injured means hurt or damaged, so the letters are knocked into a new shape

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: primarily means at first, so only the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: A single ointment, chiefly put on wounded hospital patients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'applied to' just joins the pieces; read as a whole, the clue also describes what the answer is used for.
explanation.definitionFit: An antiseptic cream is put on wounds to prevent infection, exactly what injured patients need.

clue.text: Doubles result in tennis voided

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other
voided means emptied, so only the outer letters of the word tennis remain

parts.note: a win is a result in sport

explanation.surface: A doubles match ends in a tennis result being cancelled.
explanation.definitionFit: Twins are doubles of each other, identical lookalikes.

clue.text: Verne's English physicist deprived of love by son

definitions.note: a possessive: the first name belonging to Verne, the French novelist

indicators.note: deprived of means losing something, so that letter is taken out

parts.note: James Joule was an English physicist
love is O, a nil score in tennis

explanation.surface: The French novelist's English scientist loses his love because of his son.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist who wrote Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea had the forename Jules.

clue.text: It provides a bit of help, essentially, at sea

definitions.text: It provides a bit of help, essentially, at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are thrown into disorder
the essence of a word is its core, its middle letters

explanation.surface: Something that offers some basic assistance out on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes EL from the middle of 'help'; 'at sea' rearranges A BIT OF plus EL.
explanation.definitionFit: A lifeboat is a rescue vessel that brings help to those in trouble on the water.

clue.text: Those ending tragic affair may

indicators.note: the ending of each of the following words is its final letter

explanation.surface: People who end a doomed romance might weep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending' takes the last letters of 'tragic', 'affair' and 'may'; the whole clue says such people may weep.
explanation.definitionFit: Breaking off a sad love affair may well make people weep and shed tears.

clue.text: See 9
Part of grant is ring-fenced for some weeks

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some of a grant is protected for a few weeks.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is fair because a month lasts some weeks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tisri is a month of the Jewish calendar, a period lasting about four weeks.

clue.text: No bother (almost) slicing bread in Rio

indicators.note: slicing cuts into something, so one piece goes into the middle of the other

parts.note: bread is slang for money, and in Rio de Janeiro the currency is the Brazilian real

indicators.note: almost means nearly all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: fuss means bother

explanation.surface: No trouble at all cutting a loaf in Brazil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bread' is slang for money, and Brazil's currency is the real.
explanation.definitionFit: A no is a refusal, a negative answer to a request.

clue.text: PM protected by detective and special police alarms

parts.note: DI is a detective inspector

indicators.note: something protected is surrounded, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: the SS was the Nazi special police force
Theresa May was UK prime minister

explanation.surface: A prime minister guarded by a detective and special police officers sounds the alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismay someone is to alarm or distress them, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Extract essence from processed cod etc

indicators.note: processed food is altered from its raw state, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A cook boils down fish products to get their flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: To decoct is to boil something down to extract its flavour or active ingredients.

clue.text: An old hand's adopting new protective gear

parts.note: an is the indefinite article, here giving A

indicators.note: adopting means taking in, so one letter goes within the others

parts.note: an old hand is a pro, and 's gives S

explanation.surface: An experienced worker is taking on fresh safety clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Aprons are worn over clothes to protect them from dirt or spills.

clue.text: Novel by incomer in its early stages

indicators.note: novel means new and different, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A book written by a newcomer is still at a rudimentary stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An embryonic project is undeveloped, like an embryo at the start of growth.

clue.text: It's no trouble making regular use of metal, say

indicators.note: regular use takes every other letter, the even ones here

explanation.surface: Working with metal regularly is simple enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Something easy is effortless, needing little work or fuss.

clue.text: Elusive mountain-dweller still single

parts.note: still means yet, as in yet to come
I is a single, the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The hard-to-find creature of the peaks remains unmarried.
explanation.definitionFit: The abominable snowman of the Himalayas is a legendary creature rarely, if ever, sighted.

clue.text: Soft part of foot's become very dry

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning soft
the arch is the curved section of the sole

explanation.surface: The tender bit of the foot has become cracked and dry.
explanation.definitionFit: To parch is to dry out completely through heat or thirst.

clue.text: Obscure papers ambassador's brought round

indicators.note: a piece brought round another encloses it

parts.note: HE stands for His Excellency, an ambassador's title
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: An envoy's papers were wrapped up to keep them secret.
explanation.definitionFit: To obscure something is to conceal it from view.

clue.text: Return of public transport turned out well

indicators.note: a return comes back the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: trams are a form of public transport

explanation.surface: Bringing back the trams has proved a success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out well' looks like 'went well' but means well dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well turned out is neatly and elegantly dressed, which is smart.

clue.text: Union leader in fight with editor knocked down

indicators.note: in places one piece within the other

parts.note: action is fighting, as in seeing action

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A union boss in a brawl with a newspaper editor got floored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked down' is the auctioneer's hammer coming down, not a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: At auction a lot is knocked down when the hammer falls and it is sold.
